name: CTtransit Link New Haven
note: Greater New Haven area service: New Haven and West Haven are incorporated cities (place layer); East Haven has no separate city incorporation and is encoded as its New England town (cousub layer). State-funded CTtransit microtransit connecting to Union Station rail. https://www.cttransit.com

name: CTtransit Link Stamford
note: State pilot serving Stamford (city) and Darien (town); fills gaps between corporate parks and residential areas

name: Enfield Magic Carpet Link
note: Town of Enfield; replaces fixed schedule loops

name: Meriden Microtransit
note: Zone-based city transit connecting local neighborhoods to Hartford Line commuter rail

name: New Haven Go New Haven
note: City of New Haven; pilot program testing urban demand

name: NWCTD Link
note: Service described as covering the core Torrington commercial zone, not the full city — no zone size or street boundaries published on the operator site (https://www.nwcttransit.com/); encoded as Torrington city with approximate fidelity since it is a subset of city limits. Northwestern CT Transit District also runs a 14-town Dial-A-Ride but Link is Torrington-specific.

name: Parkville Microtransit
note: Pilot in Parkville neighborhood of Hartford; likely subset of city limits

name: River Valley Transit Dial-A-Ride
note: 16-town Estuary Transit District dial-a-ride service; curb-to-curb, trips must start/end 3/4 mile beyond fixed RVT bus routes

name: Southington Microtransit
note: Town of Southington; local microtransit pilot

name: Tri-Town Connector
note: Three-town northern CT service connecting to Bradley Airport transit hub

name: Via NHV
note: App-based microtransit serving downtown and outlying urban neighborhoods; connects to Union Station rail

name: Via NHV (New Haven)
note: City of New Haven, part of CTDOT statewide pilot

name: WRTD Dial-A-Ride
note: 9-town Windham Region Transit District dial-a-ride service; available to general public with no age/disability restrictions

name: WRTD Link
note: App-based service connecting UConn Storrs (in Mansfield) to Willimantic (in Windham); covers both towns
